title: Invertibility of the finite-free evaluation transpose
statement: For l, E, L, ι, X, tensor presentations a and b, and ambient inputs K and M, the scalar-extended evaluation transpose homMap X (completedCoefficientMap l E L ι X) a b K M is an isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph 5: finite-free basis computation of the evaluation transpose.

proof.text: Use integralScalarOrdinaryModelComparison to obtain the pure-tensor-normalized ordinary scalar isomorphism t and its derived isomorphism e. Apply scalarTensor_model_comparison at K and H(K,M) to identify the scalar tensor square with the unique source and target adjoint comparisons.

Invert that tensor square, postcompose with extended evaluation, and use leftAdjointUniq_hom_app_counit. Naturality of the adjunction Hom equivalence identifies the original homMap with coefficientBaseChangeHom for the canonical closed models and the transported tensor isomorphism. Naturality of closed uncurrying shows that changing the scalar functor along e conjugates coefficientBaseChangeHom by e at the source Hom and by the target Hom functor applied to the inverse source and forward target components of e.

The canonical scalarHomOrdinary comparison is invertible by the already proved scalarHomOrdinary_isIso, which contains the finite-free basis calculation. The two components of e and the target internal-Hom image of their product are isomorphisms. Their composite, equal to the requested homMap by the preceding steps, is therefore an isomorphism.
